label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 189.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 18:28:49Z with BAD_EVENTS=retry. About 2 s later, provider event evt_000270 arrived at provider-events/2@84 with an amount that is not a positive integer of cents. ledger-consumer cannot book it. Under the retry setting it retries that same message forever, with backoff capped at 15 s, and never commits past offset 84. Every later message on partition 2 then waits behind it. Ledger lag went from 0 to 236, and the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff. payment-confirmer runs with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. It set the same event aside and kept going, so only the ledger group is stuck. Still open: where the malformed amount came from (the provider's payload, or how the receiver passed it along), and which BAD_EVENTS value ledger-consumer ran before this deploy.

evidence.shows: Consumer lag was 0 at 18:27:55, 2 at 18:28:55 and 236 at 18:29:55, still climbing.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 18:28:49Z, about 1.5 min after the rest of the stack, with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.

ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/2@84, attempts 3 to 9 through 18:29:52, error 'amount must be positive integer cents', retry interval capped at 15 s.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/2@84, at 18:28:51 for the same reason, and logged no other warnings or errors.
The trace shows event evt_000270 queued by webhook-receiver to partition 2, offset 84. payment-confirmer dead-lettered it once. ledger-consumer kept getting will_retry for 60+ s on the same offset.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before its 18:28:49 deploy, expected to be BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it sets the poison event aside and drains partition 2. Then find out why evt_000270 carries an invalid amount, check it against the provider's records, and book it by hand or replay it once corrected. The money check will report it as not posted until then.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses briefly while its container is recreated. The backlog is already blocked, so little is lost. Once the poison event is dead-lettered, the ledger will be missing evt_000270 until someone repairs it. If the earlier setting was not dead_letter, the rollback may not unblock the partition, or may change booking behavior in some other way.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). Events dead-lettered meanwhile can be replayed from the dead-letter queue.
